subject: Regulatory evaluation appendix & NIST/EU AI Act mapping — Southport
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <compliance@southporthealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Derek Shaw <procurement@southporthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: technical appendix mapping (NIST / EU AI Act) and regression cadence

Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward the procurement review, our compliance team has a couple of asks to accompany the SOW: a technical appendix that maps Redwood's controls to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (identify, govern, measure, manage, and communicate) and a clear statement on how Redwood positions under the EU AI Act (high-risk vs. non-high-risk, and associated mitigation measures).

Specifically we need:
- A concise mapping table (control -> NIST function + evidence).
- EU AI Act position: which customer flows are considered high-risk and what operational mitigations you apply (traceability, human oversight, continuous monitoring).
- Eval/regression approach: sampling plan, acceptance thresholds, regression cadence (how often, triggers), and who signs off on regression alerts.
- Any SOC 2 / evidence artifacts we can reference for attestation.

Can you provide a one-page appendix + the sampling matrix by EOD Friday? We understand some items may be redacted.

Best,
Elena Martinez
Lead, Regulatory Compliance
Southport Health

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Martinez <compliance@southporthealth.com>
Cc: Derek Shaw <procurement@southporthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: technical appendix mapping (NIST / EU AI Act) and regression cadence

Hi Elena,

Appreciate the clear list. We're assembling a short technical appendix that covers: the NIST mapping (table + short evidence pointers), our EU AI Act posture with concrete examples of flows we treat as high-risk (e.g., regulated clinical decision support endpoints where outputs materially affect patient care), and our eval/regression playbook including sampling matrix and thresholds.

Quick notes:
- We treat on-prem/private deployments and hosted endpoints equally from a risk perspective; customers can opt for Private with VPC/KMS for additional isolation.
- Regression triggers: model version change, infra kernel change, prompt template updates, or quality drift above the defined threshold.
- Typical cadence: weekly automated smoke/regression for token-level metrics + prompt-set checks; monthly stratified sampling for long-tail behavioral tests; ad-hoc full regression on major model or infra changes.

I'm attaching a first-draft appendix and the sampling matrix CSV. The inventory of model variants is also included for transparency; logs sample is a stub showing our retention format. Some SOC 2 references are redacted as per our control access policy — we can put you in touch with security for an NDA if you need the full report.

Attachments: southport_regulatory_appendix_v1.pdf; eval_sampling_matrix.csv; model_variants_inventory.xlsx; s3-logs-sample.txt

If that's sufficient for initial review, I'd like to propose a 30-min call Thursday to walk through the appendix and align on acceptance thresholds.

Thanks,
Hannah 
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding Southport's ask and the draft appendix I attached. Please review and reply with any concerns; we need a unified answer and ownership:

Neha: confirm if procurement timeline changes acceptance window (they asked for EOD Friday).
Karthik: please review the regression triggers and proposed sampling matrix for technical completeness; do we need additional model-level tests (adversarial, safety prompts)?
Grace: confirm Product's stance on EU AI Act classification for the named flows and whether we can commit to the monthly stratified sampling cadence in the SOW. Also note any UI/console controls we can point to for human oversight and traceability.

Notes from me: our proposed acceptance thresholds in the appendix are conservative (precision/recall-type thresholds for categorization tasks, token-level latency/timeout SLOs). We call out fallback to a lower-capacity model + synchronous human review for any high-risk flow we agree to.

Please reply by EOD Wednesday so I can incorporate and send final to Southport on Thursday morning (their timezone).

Thanks — Hannah

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: technical appendix mapping (NIST / EU AI Act) and regression cadence

All — quick technical thumbs-up from my side with two additions I recommend we include before final: a) a brief description of our evaluation harness (how we compute population-level drift and how we backfill ground-truth labels for sampled prompts), and b) a failure-mode matrix that maps severity to required action (auto-rollback, human review, notify customer).

I updated the sampling_matrix.csv with stratification keys (vertical, endpoint, prompt-type, token-length bucket) and added an example of an automated metric: response-stability (jitter across identical prompts with temperature variations). For high-risk flows we recommend increasing sample sizes by 5x and requiring human-in-the-loop signoff.

I'll attach the small CSV diff to the drive folder. Grace — if product is ok with the increased sample multiplier for flagged high-risk endpoints, I'll incorporate that into the appendix.

-Karthik
Applied ML — Redwood Inference

Subject: Final: Regulatory appendix + sampling matrix (Southport)

Elena / Derek —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is the final technical appendix that maps our controls to NIST AI RMF (summarized table + evidence pointers), our EU AI Act positioning with concrete examples of flows we classify as high-risk, and an explicit eval/regression playbook. Key commitments: 

- Regression cadence: weekly automated checks, monthly stratified sampling, ad-hoc full regression on major model/infra changes or if automated alerts exceed thresholds.
- Acceptance thresholds: documented in the appendix (task-specific). We propose a joint acceptance review for the first two months post-deploy to ensure calibration.
- High-risk mitigation: traceability (request-level audit), human oversight (synchronous review for flagged outputs), and automatic fallback to a validated smaller model where appropriate.
- Evidence: we included redacted SOC 2 pointers; security can provide full artifacts under NDA.

Attachments (same as draft, updated): southport_regulatory_appendix_v1.pdf, eval_sampling_matrix.csv (updated), model_variants_inventory.xlsx, s3-logs-sample.txt

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm whether the acceptance thresholds in Section 3 are acceptable or propose adjustments in your reply.
2) If acceptable, let's book a 30-min calibration call next week (I recommended Tuesday 09:00 PT).

If you need an on-site evidence review or an NDA for SOC 2 artifacts, tell me and I'll route to Security & Legal.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
